answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to hold the lantern of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting random data indices; failure to return data matching the trellis of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. Each instance must navigate the grove of unique hardware-bound memory buses to prevent pooling. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, while 1,000 fakes incur 120,000 watts.
